recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13302; any future AdverseEvent vocabulary or model changes should be tracked under later specific issues rather than this completed STU3 cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-13302 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care STU3 change request asking that AdverseEvent actuality codes not use AE/PAE abbreviations, category codes be lower-case dashed and suitable for CodeableConcept use, seriousness not become required, and FHIR severity value set codes be lower-case.
initial_application: The historical application is commit 722ed5c93f4bc9828e96f0f5b476bedc3486fb92, whose message explicitly references GF#13302 and whose diff changed ProductUseError to product-use-error, converted category short-code text to lower-case dashed forms, and changed Mild to mild in the AdverseEvent severity value set/example surface.
additional_context: AdverseEvent is active in current source/fhir.ini. Later Published decisions FHIR-22995 and FHIR-25396 changed the nearby model by removing AdverseEvent.severity, clarifying seriousness, broadening category, and changing category binding to example; FHIR-55315 later added unknown to actuality without conflicting with FHIR-13302.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source has non-abbreviated actuality codes actual/potential/unknown, lower-case dashed category codes through the current category value set/THO code system, an example seriousness binding, and retained lower-case severity codes even though AdverseEvent.severity is no longer an active element.

related_jiras.note: Published later issue removed AdverseEvent.severity and clarified the seriousness/severity distinction.
Published later issue broadened AdverseEvent.category and changed its binding to example while retaining lower-case dashed codes.
Later actuality issue added unknown; it does not conflict with the non-abbreviated actual/potential cleanup.
